blockers: Saves UI restore is nonfunctional because confirmation body is omitted.
File and metadata mutations are not fully atomic across filesystem/database failure.

evidence.outcome: Passed; Vite production build completed with existing SignalR Rollup annotation warnings.
Serialized backup lifecycle with opaque IDs, SHA-256/length metadata, temporary-file create, integrity validation, safe paths, retention, and restore rollback.
Rename/delete move or delete file before metadata update/delete; metadata persistence failure can leave inconsistent state.
List/download/restore/rename/delete routes exist; restore requires BackupRestoreRequest.Confirm and destructive handlers enforce owner role.
Saves still models backups as string[]; only create-backup and restore button exist; restore omits confirmation body and lifecycle controls are absent.

next_slice.summary: Finish Saves UI against BackupMetadata with download/owner rename-delete-restore and explicit confirmation; harden metadata/file mutation consistency with compensating cleanup or transactional strategy and focused tests.

result: Backend tests and frontend build pass, and BackupService provides metadata identity, SHA-256/length integrity validation, serialized operations, atomic temporary file creation, strict basename/containment checks, retention pruning, stopped-server guards, and restore rollback. Backend backup routes use authenticated CSRF/audit pipeline and owner checks for restore/rename/delete. The Saves UI was not completed: it still treats backups as string filenames, has no metadata/download/rename/delete controls, sends restore without required {confirm:true} body (so restore returns 400), does not show owner-only guards, and lacks restore confirmation. Metadata/file operations are not fully atomic if metadata persistence fails after file move/delete, potentially leaving orphan or mismatched state. Scheduled backup correctly skips while running.
